definitions.explanation: A school system where students attend classes during regular daytime hours on a full-time basis, as opposed to evening or correspondence programs.

examples.japanese: {全日制|ぜんにちせい}の{高校|こうこう}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: I attend a full-time high school.

examples.japanese: この{学校|がっこう}には{全日制|ぜんにちせい}と{定時制|ていじせい}の{両方|りょうほう}がある。
examples.english: This school has both full-time and part-time programs.

examples.japanese: {全日制|ぜんにちせい}の{課程|かてい}では{月曜|げつよう}から{金曜|きんよう}まで{毎日|まいにち}{授業|じゅぎょう}がある。
examples.english: In the full-time program, there are classes every day from Monday to Friday.

notes:
A compound of {全日|ぜんにち} (all day/full day) and {制|せい} (system). Most commonly used in the context of Japanese high schools, which are categorized into three types: {全日制|ぜんにちせい} (full-time), {定時制|ていじせい} (part-time/evening), and {通信制|つうしんせい} (correspondence). The vast majority of Japanese high school students attend {全日制|ぜんにちせい} programs.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全日制|ぜんにちせい}の{高校|こうこう} — full-time high school
- {全日制|ぜんにちせい}の{課程|かてい} — full-time program/course
- {全日制|ぜんにちせい}{普通科|ふつうか} — full-time general course

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {定時制|ていじせい} — part-time school system (evening school; classes typically held from late afternoon)
- {通信制|つうしんせい} — correspondence school system (distance learning)
- {夜間|やかん} — nighttime/evening (used attributively: {夜間|やかん}{学校|がっこう}, night school)
